moves.headline: SELLAS fell another 17% as it raises $150 million after its 156% jump on leukemia trial data
moves.summary: SELLAS shares more than doubled on November 17 when its cancer vaccine succeeded in a pivotal trial, and the company announced a $150 million share sale the same evening. The stock has been falling since as investors absorb the new shares.
why: On November 17, SELLAS Life Sciences said its immunotherapy galinpepimut-S met the main goal of the pivotal Phase 3 REGAL trial in acute myeloid leukemia, cutting the risk of death by 41%, with median survival of 24.0 months against 14.7 months for the best available treatment. The shares rose 156% that day, from $7.47 to $19.15.

After the close the same day, the company announced an underwritten public offering of $150 million of new shares, with an option for underwriters to buy $22.5 million more. Selling new stock straight after a surge is standard practice for a biotech that needs cash to file for approval and prepare a launch, but it adds supply and is priced at a discount.

The shares fell 6% on November 18 and a further 17% on November 19, to $14.86 — still roughly double where they stood before the data. Nothing new about the drug was announced on the day; the decline is the offering being absorbed and early buyers taking profits.
context: The trial result removes the largest risk, but not all of it. The study was relatively small, the statistical margin was not wide (p=0.035), and the company still has to agree with the FDA on what a filing requires. SELLAS has said it plans to meet the agency while preparing its application.

src.title: SELLAS announces Phase 3 REGAL results (SEC filing)
